The Quiet Grid: Editorial Restraint in Product Design

Most product interfaces shout. This session is about the ones that don't — how a magazine-trained ear for hierarchy, whitespace, and typographic rhythm can produce software that feels durable instead of decorative.

About this session

For two decades, magazines taught us that the most powerful design move is often the one you don't make. A heading set five points larger. A rule that doesn't exist. A column that holds its width because the eye needs somewhere to rest. That instinct has mostly vanished from product UI, replaced by elaborate component libraries and competing accent colors.

In this 45-minute talk, Imani walks through three case studies — a banking dashboard, a calendar app, and a CMS authoring surface — showing how editorial principles translated directly into measurable improvements in task completion and trust. We'll look at type pairing, gutter math, what "negative space" actually pays for, and the small typographic decisions that disappear into the background where they belong.

You'll leave with a framework you can apply Monday morning: a checklist for auditing a screen's noise floor, a shortlist of type stacks worth defending, and permission to delete a lot of borders.

What you'll take away
A practical "noise floor" audit — five questions to ask of any production-screen before shipping
How to defend whitespace in a stakeholder review without saying the word "breathing room"
The three type pairings that hold up across density, locale, and dark mode
A short reading list, drawn mostly from magazine design and architecture criticism
Speakers All speakers
IO
Imani Okafor
Principal Designer, Ledger & Vine · formerly The Atlantic

Imani leads brand and product design at Ledger & Vine, a small studio working with publishers and financial cooperatives. Before that, ten years as an art director on long-form editorial. She writes occasionally at quietgrid.notes.

RH
Reika Halvorsen
Independent type designer · Co-host, Type Off

Reika joins for the Q&A segment to answer the questions Imani is too polite to and to argue, gently, for serifs in software. Recent releases include the Forest superfamily and Tråg Mono.

Where to find it

Level 2 · West wing

Enter through the West Atrium, take the staircase opposite the coffee cart, and Linotype Hall is the second door on your left. Sets free across via the elevator next to the cloakroom. Live captioning provided; an induction loop is available — speak to a volunteer at the door.
